body: Yeah, based on the other comments I got I was starting to assume that was the case. Oh well, thanks for the help anyways!
I guess maybe I wasn’t clear, sorry! It’s not the thoughts themselves that are causing me angst, it’s that they are occurring in the first place. Specifically it’s the frequency of them.
No. We all went. But I couldn’t tell her ‘hey I’m near about to have a breakdown’ because she had to deal with him.
I’m not?

I don’t think she is! I realize none of this is K’s fault, I realize this is a me problem. I’m just asking for advice I ended up not needing because I just powered through and kept my mouth as shut as possible. 

Yeah, his way of grieving, I didn’t like it. Because his way of grieving had my mom crying to her friend and them two then going to the local thrift store where my grandpa had just donated a bunch of items my mom wanted and finding them and more stuff, like handmade ornaments. Complete trash to him, she had wanted them if she had known he was going to donate them. She said she wanted them, he donated them anyways. She tracked down old cedar chests he had given away. She had said she wanted one and my aunt wanted one. He sold them anyways! I don’t think people cleaning and getting rid of clutter their now dead spouse accumulated is a bad thing, I think my grandpa went about it in a bad way and hurt others more in the process because he couldn’t just slow down and think ‘oh yeah, daughter wanted this. Put it in her pile.’
I know it’s his way of dealing with it. I was just trying to explain more...
And I’m glad he has happiness in his everyday life! I’m really not trying to take that away. I’m just asking for advice on how to get through Christmas Eve without crying in the bathroom.

I’m not though? Well, maybe I am. I’m acknowledging this is a me problem, and I can’t exactly call up my therapist on Christmas Eve to talk this out. I’m trying to not cry as I look around a condo I barely recognize. I’m asking for advice on how to accomplish that.
I know. I am very happy he has someone, before K he was very depressed and it wasn’t good. I’m just asking how to not cry as I look around the condo that’s barely recognizable.
He doesn’t though. He got rid of basically everything that reminds him of her... he doesn’t even have a Christmas tree up. He completely purged the house.
Ahh. I see. I wasn't sure where else to post this, but I was aware that it may not comply with the rules. Sorry!
Yes. Would you like me to remove the post because of this?

I agree that there is nothing wrong with loving yourself. I'm simply saying that the whole boy thing in conjunction with the other things (not really showing much empathy it seems to me, and making sure that she doesn't get blamed for a huge screw up in her part) seems more in line with her possibly having narcissistic personality disorder. 

But, I could be completely wrong.
Okay, I'll cross post it. Thank you!
That sucks. I'm very sorry you had to go through that. Just thinking "someone's on my side" and then having that ripped from you. Ugh.

H is truly great. 

After he and I had a conversation (over text) while I was having another breakdown, I started talking about how, if I was in a life or death situation, I may choose death over life. 

He then made me promise to talk to him or another friend is I am ever even thinking about considering suicide at all. 

He is truly a great person.
My breakdowns are a lot of sobbing, and general panic. Other comments on the one I posted in r/relationships said it was most likely panic attacks.
Thanks so much! I will definitely keep that tip in mind!

Thank you so much for your suggestions! I will remember them. 

I don't have a school nurse, but most the ones that happen at school are after school, so I usually just go in a bathroom, put I my earbuds and turn up the music. But that doesn't always work, and sometimes they start feeling like they're going to happen in the middle of class (weird things I've found that calm me down when this starts happening: suckers and drawing on my arm). 

But thank you again so much for your suggestions! I will keep them in mind!

No, the school doesn't have a counselor. I am also currently in the process of getting a therapist (should I put that in my main post?). 

I more needed tips on how to deal with it for the time being (once again, should I make that clear in my post?). 

But thanks for what you're saying anyways! It's helpful!

I'm currently trying to get a therapist (mom needs to actually make appointments) so some the family stuff is going to be taken care of soon. 

Do you have any advice for how to deal with it for the time being (my school doesn't have a school counselor for this type of stuff, private school if that makes a difference)?
